title: Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay
summary:
The White House has issued an order extending the pause on enforcing the law targeting TikTok and similar foreign-controlled apps until December 16, 2025. During this time, the Department of Justice will not bring cases or penalties for distributing, maintaining, or updating these apps, and it will not pursue penalties for conduct that happened before now under the same law.

The order instructs the Attorney General to publish guidance and send letters to providers stating there has been no violation and no liability for actions taken during the paused period, as well as from the start of the law until this order’s date. It also makes clear that only the federal government, through the Attorney General, can investigate and enforce this law. Attempts by states or private parties to enforce it are described as encroaching on executive authority, and the Department of Justice is directed to defend that exclusive role.

This extension benefits users, creators, advertisers, small businesses, and developers who rely on TikTok for marketing and income, as well as app stores and other companies that distribute or update the app. It provides clarity and breathing room while legal and policy questions continue to play out, reducing immediate disruption to day-to-day operations and livelihoods.

Those who may see drawbacks include officials and advocates who view the app as a national security or data privacy risk and who hoped for faster enforcement. States that considered their own actions lose a path to act independently, and competitors who expected a near-term advantage could be disappointed. The order also notes it does not create new legal rights and must be carried out consistent with existing law and available funding.
